steps.title: Prepare the squid and coating
steps.text: Thaw cleaned squid in the refrigerator, drain and pat completely dry. Cut the tubes into 1/4-inch-wide rings. Beat and weigh the egg. Mix almond flour, salt, black pepper and half the garlic powder in a shallow dish. Keep the squid and egg chilled until coating.

steps.title: Mix the dipping sauce
steps.text: In a clean bowl, stir mayonnaise, lemon juice and the other half of the garlic powder. Cover and refrigerate while frying. Keep the sauce and its utensils away from raw squid and egg.

steps.title: Heat the oil
steps.text: For four servings, use a heavy 10-inch skillet with a base about 8 inches across. Use a smaller 8-inch skillet for two servings. Heat enough of the measured refined canola oil to make a shallow layer about 1/8 inch deep, reserving any rest for small top-ups between batches. Never fill the pan more than one-third deep. Heat the oil to 350°F and monitor it with a frying thermometer.

steps.title: Coat and fry in batches
steps.text: Coat only the next panful at a time: dip rings into beaten egg, let excess drain, then press lightly into the almond mixture and shake off loose flour. Fry one uncrowded layer, about four batches for four servings. Turn once after about 1 minute; allow roughly 2–3 minutes total per batch, continuing until the thickest squid reaches 145°F for at least 15 seconds and the coating is golden. Check with a thin-tip food thermometer. Oil temperature, squid thickness and coating can change the time; the endpoint decides doneness. Adjust heat to hold about 350°F and allow oil to recover before the next batch.

steps.title: Drain and serve
steps.text: Use clean tongs to transfer cooked calamari to a rack over a tray. Skim loose browned crumbs between batches with a dry slotted utensil. Serve promptly with the chilled sauce and lemon wedges. Discard remaining raw egg wash and dredge. Allow used oil to cool fully before handling or disposal.

equipment: Heavy 10-inch skillet for four servings, or an 8-inch skillet for two
Dry slotted utensil, clean tongs and a wire rack over a tray

timeline.attention: Dry the squid thoroughly; mix coating and chilled sauce.
Monitor oil continuously, turn each batch once and check the seafood endpoint.
Serve promptly; larger quantities need more batches.

tips: Almond flour browns readily. Keep the oil near 350°F, skim browned crumbs and coat each batch only when the pan is ready.
Use dry utensils around hot oil, lower rings gently away from you and keep water away from the pan.
For six or eight servings, keep the same pan and uncrowded layer; fry additional batches and reserve the extra measured oil for top-ups. Total time can increase.
recipe.fallback: If the coating browns before the squid reaches 145°F, lower the oil temperature and finish that batch to the safe endpoint. Do not use coating color or a fixed timer as proof of doneness.
limitations: This household adaptation has not been kitchen-tested; coating texture, oil use and cooking times are estimates.

Nutrition counts all measured oil, almond flour, egg wash and lemon-wedge weight even when some remain in the pan, bowl or on the plate. Actual intake can be lower; no absorption or dredge-retention measurement is claimed.
The almond-flour nutrient profile uses the established USDA whole-almond proxy. Mayonnaise and flour brands can differ. Check every packaged ingredient label for additional allergens.

nutritionEstimate.method: Measured edible cooking grams multiplied by the observed USDA SR Legacy nutrient profiles and divided into four equal portions. All measured frying oil, almond coating, egg wash, sauce and lemon wedges are counted conservatively; no oil absorption, coating retention or cooking-retention factors.
assumptions: No wheat flour, starch, sugar or carby side is in the base recipe.
All measured frying oil is counted as consumed even if left in the skillet or reserve; the cooking pan fill is not an absorption estimate.
All coating and egg wash are counted despite discarded leftovers.
The full lemon-wedge weight is counted as edible lemon flesh.
Whole-almond nutrient observations proxy the blanched almond flour; actual brands vary.
Regular USDA mayonnaise proxies the selected no-added-sugar product; actual label values and allergens may differ.

cookingSafety.decision: USDA FSIS specifies145°F for fish and shellfish during frying; FDA Food Code2022 section3-401.11(A)(1) specifies145°F for15seconds for uncomminuted fish. The350°F oil setting, ring geometry, batch times and almond coating are an untested household adaptation, not an agency recipe.
